title: Waiting for a bigger number
hook: Is "next bigger" a scan from every position?

doesNotKnow: that a stack of still-waiting values answers "next bigger to the right" in one pass

misconception: Finding the next bigger number for every position needs a scan to the right from each position: about n^2 checks.
objective: The learner can explain that a stack of numbers still waiting for a bigger one answers 'next bigger to the right' in one pass, because each number is pushed once and popped at most once: on 9 8 ... 1 it costs 8 comparisons against the scan's 36, and on 8 ... 1 9 it costs 15 even though the 9 pops eight numbers at once.

claims.text: On 9 8 7 6 5 4 3 2 1, scanning right from each position until a bigger number costs 36 comparisons (8 + 7 + ... + 1); none of them has a bigger number to its right.
claims.source: Demo.tsx run() (scanTotal), the number the question and stage print. Builder's node script (2026-10-14): 36. Closed form 8·9/2 = 36. Convention: the scan from position i compares a[i] with a[i+1], a[i+2], ... and stops at the first bigger value or the end. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): verified. Re-ran run(): scan 36 = 8+7+...+1; no answers.

claims.text: With a stack of values still waiting, 9 8 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 costs 8 comparisons: each later number is compared once with the top, which is bigger, and pushed (the first meets an empty stack).
claims.source: Demo.tsx run() (stackTotal). Convention (disclosed in the Demo.tsx header): a stack comparison is one test of the new value against the current top; the first number meets an empty stack and costs nothing. Builder's node script (2026-10-14): 8 comparisons, 0 pops. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): verified. Re-ran run(): stack 8 comparisons, 0 pops. | FC pass 25 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14, W-238): DISPUTED (off-by-one, the same as c6 had). Own run() (fc25/pops.mjs): on 9 8 ... 1 the stack costs 8 comparisons: numbers 2-9 make 1 each and the first number meets an empty stack and makes 0. The sentence says 'each new number is compared once with the top', which gives 9, not the 8 it states in the same sentence. Fix (builder): 'each later number is compared once with the top, which is bigger, and pushed (the first meets an empty stack)', matching the reveal's 'each later number'. | Builder revision v4 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14, W-239): text 'each new number' -> 'each later number ... (the first meets an empty stack)'. No stage string carried the old wording; the reveal already said 'each later number'. Builder statement, not self-verified. | FC pass 26 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Own run() (fc26-b0/pops.mjs) on 9 8 ... 1: per-number stack comparisons 0,1,1,1,1,1,1,1,1 = 8, 0 pops; the text now says each later number, the first meets an empty stack, matching both the count and the reveal.

claims.text: On 8 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 9, scanning still costs 36, and the stack costs 15: 7 comparisons while the first eight are pushed, then 8 as the 9 pops all eight waiting numbers; each of the eight gets the answer 9 and the 9 gets none.
claims.source: List added by the spec (company/design/specs/each-element-pops-once.md), not in the brief. Demo.tsx run() on LISTS[1]; builder's node script (2026-10-14): scan 36, stack 15, 8 pops, answers 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 none. 9 pushes + 8 pops = 17 <= 18. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): verified. Re-ran run() on 8 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 9: scan 36, stack 15 (7 + 8), 8 pops, answers 9 x8 then none.

claims.text: A number waits on the stack until a bigger one arrives, and then it is popped and answered, exactly once.
claims.source: The stack holds indices whose next bigger value has not been seen yet, in decreasing value from bottom to top; when a[i] arrives every smaller top is popped and answered with a[i], the first bigger value to its right (anything between them was smaller, else it would have popped it first). Each index is pushed once, so popped at most once. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): verified. Derivation checked; brute-force next-greater equals stack answers on all 5040 orders of 1..7.

claims.text: Every comparison pops a number or ends a turn, so the work grows like n, not n².
claims.source: Amortised (aggregate) count: comparisons <= pops + (n - 1), pops <= n, so comparisons < 2n; pushes + pops <= 2n. The aggregate method is CLRS 4e chapter 16 (amortized analysis; its stack MULTIPOP example uses the same argument). Scanning costs up to n(n-1)/2 (c1). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): verified. comparisons <= pops + (n-1) checked on all 5040 orders of 1..7 (max 11 for n = 7 < 2n); '9 pushes and 9 pops' is a valid (loose) bound. CLRS 4e ch. 16 amortized analysis cited from memory; not needed for the sentence. | Builder revision v6 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14, wave H r8, W-309): reveal trimmed to fit 390x844 (88 words); the '9 numbers cost at most 9 pushes and 9 pops' clause and 'stack'/'that number's' cut. Text changed, so back to unverified. Builder statement, not self-verified. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Each stack comparison either pops (at most n - 1 pops) or is the one failing test that ends a turn (at most n - 1), so comparisons <= 2n - 2. Own exhaustive check over all 40,320 orders of 1..8: comparisons = pops + stops in every case, max 13 < 16. On 9..1: 8 (0 pops, 8 stops); on 8..1 9: 15 (8 pops, 7 stops). CLRS not needed.

claims.text: Each new number pops smaller tops, then waits (stage rule line). On 8 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 9, the 9 popped all 8 waiting numbers: its row shows 8 solid 'pop' ticks labelled '8 pops'. Pressing Next number on the 9 shows its arrival, then each press pops one box, so the stack empties one box at a time down to the 9; a replay with motion on holds each pop for 260 ms (with reduced motion a replay jumps to the end); opening the reveal during a replay jumps it to the end, so the '8 pops' row and the 'scan · stack' readouts (36 · 8, 36 · 15) are on stage when the reveal opens. On 9 8 ... 1 each later number's single comparison meets a bigger top and pops nothing (a hollow 'stop' tick).
claims.source: Demo.tsx run(): the stack loop pops while the top is smaller than the new value, then pushes; on 8..1 9 step 9 has popped = 8 indices and stack = 8 comparisons (the stack is empty after the eighth pop, so no ninth test). Stage: ticks with t < popped.length are filled, the rest hollow; the label shows popped.length; the replay shows the 9's pops one frame each (pk = 0..8). Builder statement, not self-verified. | FC pass 24 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): DISPUTED. The counts hold (own run(): on 8..1 9 the 9 makes 8 comparisons, 8 pops; on 9..1 numbers 2-9 make 1 comparison each and pop nothing). But 'the stack empties one box at a time down to the 9' holds only on the replay path (All the rest, or a chip after a finished list), not with reduced motion. Reachable counter-path: choose '8 ... 1 9' first and press Next number 9 times. On the 9th press pk = null, so the stack jumps from 8 boxes to [9] in one frame, and pops-seen still fires. The reveal then says 'while the stack emptied box by box down to the 9', which that learner never saw. Fix (builder): either step the pops frame by frame on Next number too, or make the reveal clause depend on a recorded 'saw the pops replayed' flag (and handle reduced motion). Nit: on 9..1 the first number meets an empty stack (0 comparisons), so 'each number's single comparison' should say 'each later number'. | Builder revision v3 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14, W-234): Next number now steps a popping number's pops one box at a time too (the same 22 ms frames as the replay; under reduced motion one pop per press, no animation). The reveal's 'while the stack emptied box by box down to the 9' clause shows only if a recorded sawEmpty flag is set (the 9's pops were animated or stepped on 8 ... 1 9); a reduced-motion jump ('All the rest', or a chip after a finished list) does not set it. 'each number's single comparison' -> 'each later number's' (the first number meets an empty stack, 0 comparisons); the reveal's 'each new number met one bigger top' -> 'each later number'. | FC pass 25 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14, W-238): DISPUTED. The v3 mechanics hold: own state-machine port (fc25/pops.mjs) of next/rest/pick, motion on and reduced motion. Counts: on 8..1 9 the 9 makes 8 comparisons, all pops; on 9..1 numbers 2-9 make 1 comparison each, 0 pops. Stack sizes: Next number x9 (motion) 8,8,7,...,0 then [9]; reduced motion, presses 9-18 give 8 (arrival), 7,...,0, then [9]; sawEmpty is set on both paths and is not set by a reduced-motion jump (All the rest, chip after a finished list, or All the rest mid-pops). Two problems remain. (1) The claim text says 'when the 9 is stepped or replayed the stack empties one box at a time', but under reduced motion a replay jumps in one frame (replay(): reducedMotion() -> setK(N)). Fix: 'when the 9 is stepped, or replayed with motion on'. (2) Stage pointer: the reveal says 'On 8 … 1 9, look at the 9's row: 8 solid ticks marked "8 pops"', in the present tense, and the stage stays visible beside the reveal. Reachable path: chip '8 … 1 9', All the rest (pops-seen), then chip '9 8 … 1' (finished, so it replays list 0: descending-done). The reveal then opens with list 0 on stage, where the 9's row is the first row with 0 stack ticks. Fix (builder): past tense tied to the record ('the 9's row showed 8 solid ticks marked "8 pops"'), or put list 1 back on stage when the reveal opens. | Builder revision v4 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14, W-239): (1) 'stepped or replayed' -> 'stepped, or replayed with motion on' (reduced-motion replay jumps: replay() -> setK(N)). (2) Reveal pointer now past tense: 'the 9's row showed 8 solid ticks marked "8 pops"', so it reports the recorded run, not whatever list is on stage. Builder statement, not self-verified. | Builder revision v5 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14, wave G r7: pops too fast to see): Next number on a popping number now always steps one pop per press (arrival frame, then pk = 1..8, then the push), motion on or off; the replay holds each pop frame for POP_MS = 260 ms (was 22 ms for every frame). Legend 'pop' (filled) / 'stop' (hollow, thicker stroke) added beside the Stack header; the reveal names the ticks 'pop' and 'stop'. Builder statement, not self-verified. | FC pass 26 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Own run(): on 8 ... 1 9 the 9 makes 8 comparisons, all 8 pops (stack empty after the eighth, no ninth test); ticks t < popped.length are filled (pop), the rest hollow with stroke 1.8 (stop); label '8 pops'. Own port of next(): presses 1-8 place 8..1, press 9 arrival (stack 8 boxes, pk 0), presses 10-17 pop one box each (7..0, label 1 pop..8 pops), press 18 pushes 9; next() has no motion branch, so reduced motion steps the same way. play() frames for the 9: q = 0..8 then push, each q frame held POP_MS = 260 ms. replay() under reduced motion calls setK(N) (jump), sawEmpty unchanged. On 9 ... 1 numbers 2-9 make 1 comparison, 0 pops (hollow tick). 'Down to the 9' = the stack reaches 0 boxes, then [9] is pushed. | Builder revision v6 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14, wave H r8, W-309): stage rule line shortened to 'Each new number pops smaller tops, then waits.' (one line at 390 px). Reveal sentence now 'On 8 … 1 9, the 9 popped all 8 waiting numbers ("8 pops", solid ticks): 15 in all, against 36.'; the sawEmpty 'while the stack emptied box by box down to the 9' clause is cut (state removed). Milestone pops-seen now fires when the 9 arrives in a replay (about 270 ms after the chip), not at the end of the ~2.6 s replay, so the reveal can open while the 9's pops are still playing (they finish within about 2.3 s); the sentence shows on that record (popsSeen) or the filled readout. Picture labels raised to 12 px (render >= 10 px at 390 px). Text and timing changed, so back to unverified. Builder statement, not self-verified. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. v6 code read: next() on the 9 of 8..1 9 gives the arrival frame (pk 0, 8 boxes), then one pop per press (7..0 boxes, labels '1 pop'..'8 pops'), then the push of 9; play() holds each pop frame POP_MS = 260 ms; replay() under reduced motion jumps (setK(N)); OnReveal calls snapToEnd, which clears the timer and finish()es the list if a replay is running. Ticks t < popped.length are filled ('pop'), the rest hollow with stroke 1.8 ('stop'). On 9..1 each later number makes 1 comparison, 0 pops. Nit, non-blocking: if both lists are done and the learner picks 9 8 … 1 again (a replay) and opens the reveal, the '8 pops' row is not on stage; the reveal sentence is past tense and the readouts '36 · 8' and '36 · 15' are, so nothing false is shown.

recall.question: A one-pass stack answers 'next bigger to the right' for 1,000 numbers. At most about how many stack comparisons can it make?
recall.why: Each number is pushed once and popped at most once, and every comparison either pops a number or ends a turn, so the work is under 2 x 1,000. Scanning from every position can cost about 500,000.
